body: I don't think this scenario has come up before. Putting the unknown option into a hidden input would make radio() work differently than select(), and checkbox() which I'm not a fan of. If we made all the methods consistent we could make a change.

@markstory The idea wouldn't be to put the unknown option into the hidden field, but to effectively get the hidden field with an empty value in order to prevent the black-hole. 

Currently as the hidden field is missing, if no option is manually selected, the field is not posted at all, making the Security component block the request. Thus clicking the submit button just after the page has loaded results in a black-hole.
@alaxos I agree. The input should always at least post an empty string here.
@alaxos ok I wasn't clear on what you wanted/expected. I agree that including the empty input is reasonable.

issue.title: Always output the radio hidden field if its enabled.

repository.name: cakephp
repository.description: CakePHP: The Rapid Development Framework for PHP - Official Repository

issue.body:
Always include hidden input on radio buttons if the option is set. There can exist conditions where the value is not in the available options. In these situations, the generated inputs did not submit a value, which can cause issues with SecurityComponent.

Refs #6771
